newsitem.title: USA: Clinton says he will press Congress to back Mexico.
newsitem.headline: Clinton says he will press Congress to back Mexico.

text.p: President Clinton said Monday he would do his best to convince Congress to back his decision to certify Mexico as an ally in the war against drugs.

"We're going to make a full court press to bring the administration's position and perspective to the members of Congress ...," Clinton said at a joint White House news conference with Egyptian President Hosni Mubarak.

Last week the House International Relations Committee voted 27-5 to overturn Clinton's finding that Mexico was fully cooperating in the anti-drug fight. The full House is expected to take up the measure this week.
A similar measure has been introduced in the Senate and the Foreign Relations Committee has scheduled a hearing on the issue for Wednesday.

Under a 1961 law, congressional disapproval of Clinton's certification that Mexico is an anti-drug ally automatically triggers a ban on U.S. aid and requires votes against multilateral development bank assistance to Mexico.
Clinton defended his decision to certify Mexico as an ally and said he believed the government is cooperating and noted several actions that had been taken.
"I'm going to do my best to persuade the Congress that we're right," Clinton said.
